text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH 5xx spike detected in us-east-1 (infra/ingress). Error rate +420% vs baseline. Affected backend: text-gen-v2. Alert ID: INC-2026-218001. Link: https://console.ops/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-218001 :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: I'm on it. Investigating now — grabbing traces and recent deploys.

ben_sre: seeing provider A (edge-us-east-a) egress errors around the same time. Herding metrics now. Is traffic still going to provider A only?

carla_platform: routing table shows us-east primary -> provider A, fallback -> provider B (lower capacity). No recent routing deploys in last 2h.

alice_oncall: traces show 502/504 upstream from provider A's proxy pool. Latency for successful requests normal. Likely provider-side degradation, not model.

dan_product: any customer-facing errors? Is this hitting paid tenants?

elaine_support: a handful of premium customers opened tickets with timeouts. Not widespread but a few high-importance accounts impacted.

ben_sre: plan proposal: 1) apply short-term rate-limits for anonymous/free traffic and lower-priority routes; 2) shift a portion of capacity to provider B; 3) brownout non-critical features (autosuggest, proactive-caching) to reduce steady-state load. Can we implement in that order?

alice_oncall: agree. Start with rate-limits and feature toggle, then incrementally shift traffic. I'll own orchestration. Ben, can you prepare the routing change?

carla_platform: rate-limit config snippet to apply to ingress (example):
```json
{
  "scope": "us-east",
  "rules": [
    {"matcher": "tier:free", "qps": 5},
    {"matcher": "route:/embed", "qps": 10}
  ]
}
```
Apply via configctl: `configctl apply --file us-east-rate-limits.json`

alice_oncall: applying rate-limits to free tier now.

alice_oncall: ✓ applied rate-limits to free tier and embed routes. Observing...

ben_sre: starting feature brownout for autosuggest in us-east (non-prod flag path). Doing gradual rollout 0 -> 100 over 2 mins. Command: `ffctl rollout --flag autosuggest --region us-east --pct 100 --reason "incident mitigation"`

dan_product: thumbs up to brownout. That feature is low value for premium customers so should be safe.

elaine_support: posting a one-liner to impacted customers: "We're throttling lower-priority traffic in us-east to restore stability; premium API access should be unaffected. Follow-up in ~15m."

frank_netops: preparing provider reroute. We'll shift 30% of us-east traffic to provider B initially. Routing update: modify weights in service mesh:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: TrafficSplit
metadata:
  name: us-east-textgen
spec:
  backends:
    - name: provider-a
      weight: 70
    - name: provider-b
      weight: 30
```
Applying via `kubectl apply -f us-east-traffic-split.yaml`

ben_sre: before changing weights, add a small circuit-breaker to provider B to catch errors: `upstream.max_conns=200, upstream.max_pending=50`

frank_netops: applying traffic-split now. Will monitor.

frank_netops: ✓ traffic-split applied. provider-b now at 30% weight. Monitoring logs and 5xx rates.

alice_oncall: initial degradation down from +420% to +90% in 3m. Good trend. Keep steady, continue to observe.

ben_sre: noticed some increased latency hitting provider B but error rate lower. Keeping circuit-breaker in place.

carla_platform: rolling window metrics show request success rate improving for premium routes. Free-tier still rate-limited.

elaine_support: updating customer comms: "We've implemented mitigations and are seeing improvements. We'll update again in 20 minutes."

dan_product: request to hold any new deploys to inference infra in us-east until stabilised.

alice_oncall: agreed — blocking deploys via deploy-bot for us-east. `deploy-bot: hold`

incident-bot: Update: Incident INC-2026-218001 status -> mitigated. Current 5xx spike reduced to baseline+15%. Paging suppressed.

alice_oncall: handing off to ben_sre for the 2h watch. I need to jump to another pager. Ben — you're the primary now.

ben_sre: taking over. I'll keep the runbook open and watch error budgets. Please slack me if anything flips.

frank_netops: plan for next steps (ben): 1) if stable for 30m, reduce provider-b weight back to 10%; 2) revert feature brownout only after verifying premium latencies; 3) keep rate-limits until traffic normalizes for 2 consecutive 10m windows.

ben_sre: acknowledged. Also will open a post-incident ticket to vendor-provider A support and attach traces.

alice_oncall: TL;DR: provider A partial outage -> applied targeted rate-limits, brownout non-critical feature, shifted 30% traffic to provider B. Impact: a few premium customers had timeouts early but were largely mitigated after failover. Handoff to ben for monitoring and vendor follow-up.

elaine_support: adding ticket updates for affected customers and linking this thread.

carla_platform: created runbook entry and a shortplay to automate the rate-limit + brownout sequence for future similar events. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/mitigations/pull/142

ben_sre: thanks everyone. I'll post final status and RCA pointer when we have vendor response.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-218001 -> recorder note added by ben_sre. Opportunity: consider automated fallback to provider B at 15% on first alert.

frank_netops: noted. I'll file a task to prototype auto-failover with gradual ramp and health checks.

ben_sre: closing active pager but keeping watch for 2 hours. If anyone sees regressions, ping me directly. :eyes:
